title: H.B. 5222 — An Act Concerning Consumer Protection, Cannabis, Data Privacy, Fire Inspections, Criminal Mischief And Artificial Intelligence.
mechanism: Sec. 46 (effective Oct 1, 2026): no subscription-based provider shall enter into or renew a subscription, or collect a fee, without written notice of key terms and the consumer's written acceptance; enforced solely by the Attorney General, with no private right of action. Sec. 47 (effective Oct 1, 2027): the Department of Consumer Protection shall develop and administer a pilot program approving independent verification organizations; their evidence is admissible only in private injury or property damage suits, with no presumption in Attorney General or state enforcement. The pilot terminates March 31, 2031.
thresholds: Sec. 46: generative AI systems with more than one million users per month, offered to consumers by subscription. Sec. 47: covers artificial intelligence models assessed for adherence to best-practice standards.
penalties: Violation of Sec. 46(b) is an unfair or deceptive trade practice under section 42-110b(a); enforced solely by the Attorney General; section 42-110g does not apply. No private right of action.
status_text: Status: Introduced Feb 18, 2026; Signed by the Governor (June 2, 2026)
